topics.topic: Whether post-exit scratch usage above the limit independently counts as a resource hit
questions: Must a post-exit scratch total above the constant be a resource hit even when the environment was not killed for it and no qualifying OSError escaped, or must the latter note be changed to include the new post-exit measurement?

Must a post-execution scratch total above the constant be a resource hit, or must scratch count as hit only when the environment was killed for it or an uncaught MemoryError/OSError reached the parent?

Must a post-exit scratch total above the constant count as a resource hit even though the environment was not killed for it and no OSError escaped, or must the later exhaustive conditions be changed to include that post-exit measurement?

quotes: the scratch total by the parent, measured once when the environment has ended — the st_size of each distinct regular file (by inode) under the exchange directory, the files the parent put there excluded, directories and symbolic links counting nothing and a file removed before the end not counted — a total above that constant being a resource hit

A memory, scratch or output bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it from outside: the environment was killed for it, or a MemoryError, or an OSError for a full or over-limit exchange directory, escaped run and reached the parent through the exchange channel; code that catches such an error and returns is judged by what it returned, like any other output (owner, 2026-10-06).
judgement.why: One passage makes the post-exit scratch measurement independently establish a resource hit, while the other limits a scratch hit to killing or an escaped qualifying error.
